N. Gadgil Jewellers Limited''', also known as '''Purshottam Narayan Gadgil Jewellers''', is an Indian [[jewellery]] company founded by Ganesh Gadgil in Sangli in 1832. It is one of the oldest jewellery companies in India,{{Cite web |title=P N Gadgil Jewellers hits 10% upper circuit on dazzling Q3 show; PAT up 49% |url=https://www.business-standard.com/markets/news/p-n-gadgil-jewellers-hits-10-upper-circuit-on-dazzling-q3-show-pat-up-49-125021300622_1.html |website=Business Standard}} known for its production of jewellery distinctive to the Maharashtra.{{cite book |last1=Sabyasachi |first1=Dasgupta |title=Optimizing Millennial Consumer Engagement With Mood Analysis |last2=Priya |first2=Grover |date=20 July 2018 |publisher=IGI Global |isbn=978-1-5225-5691-6 |page=195 |language=en}} As of 2025, the company is headquartered in Pune and operates 53 retail stores, including 52 in [[Maharashtra]] and [[Goa]] and one in [[California]], US.{{Cite web |date=2025-03-26 |title=PNG Jewellers strengthens retail footprint with store in Pune |url=https://in.fashionnetwork.com/news/Png-jewellers-strengthens-retail-footprint-with-store-in-pune,1714406.html |access-date=2025-06-27 |website=FashionNetwork.com |language=en-IN}} == History == === Early years (1832–1890) === The company was founded as Gadgil Jewellers on 29 November 1832 by Ganesh Gadgil in Sangli. In its early years, the business operated without a permanent storefront and was initially run from a pavement in a busy part of the city.{{cite book |last1=Joshi |first1=P. K. |title=Gadgil Kulavruttanta |date=1989 |location=[[Pune]] |page=93 |language=mr |trans-title=The Gadgil Family Genealogy Almanac}}{{cite news |last1=Deshpande |first1=Renuka |date=11 September 2011 |title=Gadgil Jewellers 179-year-old journey from footpath to international showrooms |url=https://www.dnaindia.com/mumbai/report-gadgil-jewellers-179-year-old-journey-from-footpath-to-international-showrooms-1586102 |work=[[Daily News and Analysis|DNA]] |language=en}} In 1860, Gadgil relocated the business to a waada (traditional residence) he had purchased in [[Sangli]].{{sfnp|Joshi|1989|page=93}} Under Gadgil's father, the family had previously served as [[Moneylender|''savakars'']] to the Kolhatkar and Modak families of the [[Sangli State|Princely state of Sangli]], and were thus accorded the office of [[Crown Jeweller|royal jeweller]] to the [[Patwardhan dynasty|Patwardhan]] kings of the State after the establishment of their jewellery business.{{sfnp|Joshi|1989|pages=93, 95}} === 1890–1958 === Although Gadgil intended all three of his sons to participate in the business, it was eventually continued by his middle son Narayan Gadgil. His other sons, Ramchandra and Gopal, pursued careers in moneylending and law, respectively. In 1874, Ganesh Gadgil renamed the business P. N. Gadgil Jewellers after his grandson, Purshottam Narayan Gadgil.{{sfnp|Joshi|1989|pages=95}} Following Ganesh Gadgil’s death in 1890, Narayan Gadgil and his sons managed the company. After Narayan’s death in 1920, management passed to Purshottam Gadgil and his brothers, Ganesh Gadgil II and Vasudev Gadgil. Upon Purshottam’s death in 1954, the business continued under the leadership of the extended family’s next generation.{{sfnp|Joshi|1989|pages=95–97}}{{cite book |last1=Bhargava |first1=Gopal K. |title=Land and People of Indian States and Union Territories: In 36 Volumes. Maharashtra |last2=Bhatt |first2=S. C. |date=2006 |publisher=Gyan Publishing House |isbn=978-81-7835-372-2 |page=336 |language=en |quote=P. N. Gadgil and Company - Licence and Address}}{{Cite web |title=Gadgil Jewellers 179-year-old journey from footpath to international showrooms |url=https://www.dnaindia.com/mumbai/report-gadgil-jewellers-179-year-old-journey-from-footpath-to-international-showrooms-1586102 |access-date=2024-08-06 |website=DNA India |language=en}} === Expansion to Pune (1958–2012) === In 1938, Anant Gadgil, the younger son of Ganesh Gadgil II, joined the family business and worked at the Sangli store for nearly two decades. In 1958, he and his cousin, the son of Vishwanath Gadgil, established a new retail outlet in Pune under the name P. N. Gadgil Jewellers & Company, located on Laxmi Road.{{sfnp|Joshi|1989|pages=95–97}} This marked the beginning of operations in two locations under the same brand. The Pune branch was managed by Anant, Vishwanath Gadgil, and Laxman Gadgil, while the Sangli branch was overseen by Hari, the son of Vasudev Gadgil, and Shankar, Anant’s elder brother.{{sfnp|Joshi|1989|pages=96–99}} Following the death of Vasudev Gadgil in 1965, the Sangli branch continued under the management of his descendants.{{sfnp|Joshi|1989|pages=98}}{{cite book |title=Bulletin of the Institution of Engineers (India). |date=1979 |publisher=[[Institution of Engineers (India)]] |location=[[University of Illinois at Urbana-Champaign]] |page=13 |language=en |quote=P N Gadgil & Co, Jewellers of Poona}} === Formal separation and IPO (2012–present) === In 2012, the Pune and Sangli branches formally separated, with the Pune operations continuing under the name P. N. Gadgil & Company. After Anant Gadgil's death in 2014, his son and grandson, including Saurabh Gadgil, inherited a portion of the business.{{cite news |date=11 January 2014 |title=P N Gadgil Jewellers founder 'Dajikaka' dead |url=https://indianexpress.com/article/cities/pune/p-n-gadgil-jewellers-founder-dajikaka-dead/ |work=[[The Indian Express]] |language=en |quote=Three founders of the P N Gadgil Jewellers are dead. others branches are owned by Akshay and Rohan, grandsons of Laxman and Ajit, son of Vishwanath.}}{{cite book |last1=Pahwa |first1=Saloni |title=Haute Brides & Honeymoons |date=January 2016 |publisher=Pioneer Book Co. Pvt. Ltd. |page=71 |language=en}} Saurabh Gadgil, who had joined the company in 2000, later became its chairman and managing director. During his tenure, the company was restructured as a corporate entity.{{Cite news |last=Palepu |first=Advait |date=17 October 2024 |title=Jeweler Becomes Billionaire After 192-Year-Old Indian Firm's IPO |url=https://www.bloomberg.com/news/articles/2024-10-17/heir-to-192-year-old-indian-jewelry-empire-becomes-billionaire |publisher=Bloomberg News}} In September 2024, the company held an [[Initial public offering|IPO]] that raised approximately ₹1,100 crore. It was subsequently listed on the [[Bombay Stock Exchange]] and the [[National Stock Exchange of India|National Stock Exchange]].{{Cite web |title=PN Gadgil Jewellers IPO: What GMP signals ahead of share listing date |url=https://www.livemint.com/market/ipo/pn-gadgil-jewellers-ipo-what-gmp-signals-ahead-of-share-listing-date-11726478817052.html}}{{Cite web |title=PN Gadgil Jewellers IPO listing date today. GMP, experts indicate strong debut of shares on BSE, NSE |url=https://www.livemint.com/market/ipo/pn-gadgil-jewellers-ipo-listing-date-today-gmp-experts-indicate-strong-debut-of-shares-on-bse-nse-11726539144080.html |website=Live Mint}} Following the IPO, the Gadgil family retained a majority ownership stake in the firm. == Operations == PNG Jewellers uses a combination of company-owned and franchise-operated stores. In 2014, PNG Jewellers established a diamond manufacturing unit in [[Mumbai]].{{Cite web |date=2014-12-24 |title=पी. एन. गाडगीळ ज्वेलर्सचे हिरेजडीत दागिने निर्मितीत |url=https://www.loksatta.com/arthasatta/p-n-gadgil-jewellers-sets-up-diamond-manufacturing-unit-1054306/ |access-date=2024-02-29 |website=[[Loksatta]] |language=mr}} As of 2025, PNG Jewellers operated 53 outlets, including 52 stores across 21 cities in Maharashtra and Goa, and one store in the United States.{{Cite web |title=Strengthening retail presence with trust |url=https://ftp.motilaloswal.com/emailer/Research/PNGJL-20241208-MOSL-ICPG038.pdf |website=Motilal Oswal Research report}} Of the total, 41 stores were company-owned, while 12 operated under the FOCO model.{{Cite web |title=Announcement under Regulation 30 (LODR)-Investor Presentation |url=https://www.bseindia.com/xml-data/corpfiling/AttachLive/8df535b2-b24c-414d-bdf6-eec58ce58920.pdf |access-date=2025-05-15 |website=BSE India |language=en}} == References == {{reflist}} == External links == {{Sister project links|wikt=no|commons=no|commonscat=no|n=no|q=no|s=no|b=no|v=no|species=no|d=yes|m=no|mw=no}} * {{Official website|https://www.pngjewellers.com|P.
